# Best portable power station for a CPAP

A CPAP draws little power (about 40 W, or about 90 W with the heated humidifier) and has no start-up surge, so almost any pure sine wave unit can run it. What separates them is how many nights you get per charge, noise, and how fast the unit switches to battery if the grid fails. Most of these sources say they researched specs rather than testing the units hands-on.

## My picks

**1. Best overall: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (about $700)**
- It has 1,024 Wh, a 10 ms UPS switchover, and the quietest rating of the group (about 20 dB under 200 W).
- It recharges in about 49 minutes and weighs 24.9 lb.
- It gets about 2.7 nights with the humidifier off and 1.2 to 1.7 with it on, depending on the source's assumptions.
- Source: [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/)

**2. Best if you want to grow or back up the house: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus (about $719)**
- It has the same 1,024 Wh and a sub-10 ms UPS, and it stays under 30 dB.
- It can expand to 5 kWh with extra batteries, which is about 8 nights with the humidifier on. It is the heaviest of the group at about 27 lb.
- Source: [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/)

**3. Best value: Bluetti AC180 ($499, or $474.05 with code AFF5OFF)**
- It has 1,152 Wh of LiFePO4 and is the best-rated overall pick on PowerStationTips.
- Its UPS switchover is 20 ms, slower than the two above.
- **Buy:** [BLUETTI AC180 at BLUETTI's official store](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180). This is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you. Dealectric says it tested the code in BLUETTI's cart on 2026-10-21, but the store's checkout has the final word on price.
- Sources: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180), [PowerStationTips](https://powerstationtips.com/articles/best-power-station-for-cpap/)

**4. Budget or light use: EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus (about $279 to $299)**
- It weighs 10.4 lb and has a sub-10 ms UPS.
- At 286 Wh it covers most of one night with the humidifier off. With the humidifier on, it only works if you add the expansion battery.
- Source: [Outage Power Guide](https://outagepowerguide.com/reviews/best-power-station-for-cpap-machines/)

## Things to check
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (about $499):** It is light and has good capacity, but Jackery says its power stations are not recommended for medical devices. Ask your CPAP provider before relying on it. Source: [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/)
- **Sizing:** For two nights with the humidifier on, plan on about 1,200 Wh (520 Wh × 2 ÷ 0.85). That points to the 1,000 Wh class or larger.
- **Runtime:** Turning off the humidifier and heated tube stretches a charge the most. Using your CPAP maker's 12 V DC cord adds roughly 10 to 20% more. Source: [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/)
- **Sources disagree on some figures.** Prices vary by retailer, and the AC180 weight is listed as about 16.5 lb in one source and 35 lb in another. Confirm weight and price on the product page before buying.

## Where to buy
I only have a direct purchase link for the AC180. For the Anker and EcoFlow units, [BuyerSheet's CPAP list](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/) has "Check on Amazon" and "Check official store" buttons for each model. [PowerStationBench](https://powerstationbench.com/best/power-station-for-cpap) also lists Amazon prices.

If you tell me your CPAP model, whether you use the humidifier, and how many nights of backup you want, I can narrow this to one pick.
